{{verse|chapter=27|verse=21}} And vvhen there had been long fa{{ls}}ting, then Paul {{ls}}tanding in the middes of them, {{ls}}aid, You {{ls}}hould in deede, O ye men, haue heard me, and not haue parted from Crete, & haue gained this hurt and lo{{ls}}{{ls}}e. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=22}} And novv I exhort you to be of good cheere. for there {{ls}}hal be no lo{{ls}}{{ls}}e of any {{ls}}oule among you, but of the {{ls}}hip. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=23}} For {{sup|‖}} an Angel of the God vvho{{ls}}e I am, and {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''{{lang|grc|ᾧ λατρεύω}}''.}}∷ vvhom I {{ls}}erue, {{ls}}toode by me this night, {{verse|chapter=27|verse=24}} {{ls}}aying, Feare not Paul, thou mu{{ls}}t appeare before Cæ{{ls}}ar: and behold God hath {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Paul ({{ls}}aith S. Vvhereby he proueth that if God do much for the merits of Saincts in this life, much more at their interce{{ls}}{{ls}}ion & praier in heauen.}}∷ giuen thee al that {{ls}}aile vvith thee. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=25}} For the vvhich cau{{ls}}e be of good cheere ye men: for I beleeue God, that it {{ls}}hal {{ls}}o be, as it hath been {{ls}}aid to me. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=26}} And vve mu{{ls}}t come vnto a certaine iland. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=27}} But after the fourtenth night vvas come on vs, as vve vvere {{ls}}ailing in Adria about midnight, the {{ls}}hipmen deemed that there appeared {{ls}}ome countrie to them. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=28}} Vvho al{{ls}}o {{ls}}ounding, found tvventie fadomes: and being parted a litle from thence, they found fiftene fadomes. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=29}} And fearing le{{ls}}t vve {{ls}}hould fall into rough places, ca{{ls}}ting out of the {{ls}}terne foure ankers, they vvi{{ls}}hed<noinclude>{{continues|that}}</noinclude>
